My approach to writing proposals is more about simplicity rather than over detailed proposals. The value is in the delivery not in the proposal itself. 

If we were requesting 300m EDG it would require a longer and more detailed proposal. But this proposal is less than $15k so the time i spend writing this needs to be concise. 

Btw, this proposal is not a draft. 

I don't how I can find the time to answer all the questions right now, but i will try to on the next Thursday dev call, which will be recorded.

W3F do ask for a budget, per milestone. And this is the Milestone 1 budget. I feel that it is very reasonable, given the funding request. 

_Update:_ More granular breakdown shared through the RC invoice. 

Ramsey(Decentration) funding as [Product Manager](https://productmanagerhq.com/what-is-a-product-manager/) is not included in this proposal. 
And Eljo funding also not included.

Getting people (not treasury) to subscribe as opposed to just send multiple manual transactions or using the scheduling pallet is maybe not really something that ought to live in the runtime, but rather at app level.

full_text:
Getting people (not treasury) to subscribe as opposed to just send multiple manual transactions or using the scheduling pallet is maybe not really something that ought to live in the runtime, but rather at app level.

For treasury/democracy, this is different: providing recurring payments based on community funds is a widespread usecase, there are already a few projects who have implemented this functionality (or very closely related ones like continuous vesting, which is practically equivalent). Even our own treasury reward pallet has a mechanism to provide this, even though it is not really useful since based on a percentage of the treasury printing than on a fixed amount. But it could be easily amended. 
 
Though, those usually implement that as part of more  complex pallets, since this is a rather simplistic functionality and the number of pallets that a runtime can deal with is limited. 
Right now, recurring payments on treasury appears like some nice first project for someone willing to learn how to build a pallet, so I would rather see it proposed as a small bounty to encourage someone willing to try it first time and go through the tutorials. 

Last, it would be really useful to get an idea of how much you think this functionality is needed and of how you see it used.
The concept of recurring payments is really appealing, they provide payees with a predictable income, and they simplify the actions that payers need to conduct by optimistically (tacitly) re-conducting payments, till any party decides it does not want to go on with the contract.
In blockchain projects with governance, it is unrealistic expect a vote every single month, so the way it is currently solved is to entrust a smaller party (administrators, curators, multisig, etc.) to recover efficiency and proceeds regularly the payments on behalf of the community. 
This has the downside of relying on trust, or partial trust of members of the set, that acts as a local centralization point. Getting rid of those centralization points is a compelling objective, but only so long as it can retain their benefits.
For instance, let's take the issue of having to cancel a subscription if the payee starts to misbehave: the pallet could either: 1/ rely on a small set of administrators and we are no better than a multisig or 2/ rely on onchain governance, with the downside that it could be very hard to coordinate people to do that on the short term should any misbehaving contractor requiring to be stopped.

Overall, as any balance between trust/centralization and efficiency can be struck by changing the singing threshold, and that the costs of getting funds stolen a required majority of signers corrupt can be mitigated by funding the multisig with smaller amounts, it seems that they are just an easier and more efficient way to achieve the same. This is (amongst other things) why the edgeware treasury reward funding has never been used in practice, and also why projects that thought or implemented this functionality rarely turned out to use it in practice.

Yes that's absolutely not the main use case. Main use case is people able to subscribe to other people's service, with recurring automated monthly payments.

Few thoughts / questions:

-----

- This is the third pallet collab between Decentration and Rusty Crewmates. Would be interesting if you shared some learnings so far... what has been easy, what has been hard? Just a general sum-up from you and RC that might be useful for those that follow...


- With _PalletMint and PalletSupersig _can you speak to how composability can work between the calls made between the pallets, or any ideas for how this develops and maybe a simple flow diagram of how a process might evolve?


- As I currently understand it, _PalletSubscription_ will work only into PalletSuperSig, or will it be compatible with the existing PalletMultisig? ie for teams not using SuperSig, can they use it?


- Can we wire this up directly to work with the existing _PalletDemocracy_ and PalletTreasury to enable Subscriptions executed via SimpleMajority proposals or does this have to all be routed through an 'L1' account?


- Further to that, will this work directly with Kabocha's _PalletMint _or does it still require the second hop?


Those are my main technical / process questions, the following is a more general point on costs / funding / structures. 

- The funding request is for 7.8M EDG - the previous PalletSuperSig was 10M EDG, is there any logic you can share that gives some sort of outline budget?  Right now it is hard to guage and in general I believe we should be moving to increasing levels of transparency around proposals funding simply because without this context, it is very hard to replicate for new teams / proposals. 


- Given all proposals and funding is on-chain and public it seems sensible to just be up front about costs and to make the case with a basic budget. 


A push back to this might be that W3F don't request budgets, however the counter to this is they are sitting on a massive treasury (which we don't) and have expert curators making decisions and use a very rigid template which filters the key information up front - something we don't have yet. 

Right now we have an emerging network of 'curators' and then a collective who mandate funding via their votes and it is paramount that we 'level up' the education and understanding of our holders (those who vote) so they can make educated and informed decisions.

The onus is therefore on the more experienced contributors - Decentration, Decent Partners, SCU, Agency to advance proposal standards and processes and ask difficult questions where appropriate of each other - the ability to be honest and open is a duty of colleagues / peers  and is how we build strong foundations together for others to build on.

- The 7.8m EDG is:  the budget breakdown which is shared in the proposal + NSP fee. 


- There is a slight buffer between dollar and EDG, but in future invoices will be made in EDG to be exacting. 


- Ramsey(Decentration) as Product Manager and Eljo are unpaid in this funding proposal, which will be made in separate proposals. 


- [@Shankar Warang](/edgeware/account/jA7pLH65zgRNA4UgwqHEWWRxTgg51wuAUgfzmZoYWM2dMVS) also asked for this and it is now updated.

Thanks for this [@Decentration](/edgeware/account/mHDNswFgLQiiXGwkWCXgpwE27eppYppa96cMNWzT2kQF27z) really helpful. (I'd redact their bank account details).

So RC are invoicing Decentration, and Decentration are invoicing EDG. This is good and clear and similar to how I've ended up with some stuff.

Are they expecting $$$ from you or EDG? 

Add in the7 day moving average which is $ 0.0017 per EDG. (01/07/22)

So that's a total invoice (7.8m EDG) of $13260 equivalent, with 10% NSF included = $1326 for Decentration.

Working backwards:

Total invoice $13260 - 1326 - $11400 (RC invoice) = $534 

Is this $534 for your time or a small contingency as you mention?

One thing I'd say based on seeing RC invoice, is you should be adding a line for your / Decentration time if you are working on this?

Its a balance with the NSF fee, it should really be your margin, but not at the expense of where you dedicate real time.

So I'd encourage you to bump up your fee and make clear your lines.

> Are they expecting $$$ from you or EDG?
From Decentration as it is underwritten. Sharing of details such as invoices may only be a one-off given that the disclosure of all information from a private entity is not obliged. 

> $534
This buffer was larger than this at the start of the process. Hopefully it is sufficient to cover the invoice, else will have to do more admin to pay the discrepancy. The remaining buffer funds can be returned to treasury / accounted for. 

Sidenote: It would be great if invoices were in EDG so that the price has no currency risk. But of course not all contractors would be interested. Though im sure RC would. 

> One thing I'd say based on seeing RC invoice, is you should be adding a line for your / Decentration time if you are working on this?
Will be making a proposal for my contribution in a separate proposal, which is not just `pallet_subscription`.
